committeeQuestion.question: If several agents respond to the same liquidity signal, what evidence shows their combined behaviour will not create avoidable payment delays or gridlock?
committeeQuestion.why: BIS Project Agenti is testing how different agent objectives and strategies may affect payment timing, liquidity use and shock propagation in a controlled simulator.
committeeQuestion.evidence: A scenario showing the agents’ objectives, payment priorities, liquidity buffers, common signals, queue effects and trigger for human intervention.

committeeQuestions.question: Which critical payment or orchestration service would stop several agents at once, and can the firm restore minimum service if its normal control plane is unavailable?
committeeQuestions.why: Agent interactions can amplify a shared dependency failure. The test should include containment and recovery as well as prevention.
committeeQuestions.evidence: A dependency map, a tested manual or independent fallback, recovery-time evidence and the named decision owner for switching to minimum service.

committeeQuestions.question: What independent evidence supports the provider’s claims about agent performance, limitations and safeguards in the workflow we plan to use?
committeeQuestions.why: This week’s model launches and Anthropic’s METR arrangement show that capability and access to assurance evidence are changing, while provider claims still need attribution and challenge.
committeeQuestions.evidence: An evaluation report with scope, access limits, tested failure modes, publication terms, unresolved findings and the accountable reviewer.

judgement.title: When agents interact, resilience becomes a system test.
judgement.editorialAngle: Test collective behaviour in shared payment and service systems, where individually controlled agents can still create correlated delays and make recovery harder.
judgement.distinctFromPrevious: Edition 17 asked whether a firm's evidence could reconstruct one agent's unintended action. Edition 18 moves to the system around the agent: how multiple participants may interact through shared payment, liquidity and service dependencies, and whether the firm can contain and recover from their combined effects.
judgement.observation: BIS Project Agenti tests how agents with different objectives affect payment timing, liquidity, gridlock and shock propagation. Japan's finance minister says G7 finance ministers and central bank governors agreed to tabletop exercises on AI-driven cyberattacks; no design or dates are specified.
judgement.executiveJudgement: Test agent interaction. Different objectives can shift payment timing or liquidity together. Losing a shared payment or orchestration service could compound outcomes. September's FPC record links frontier-AI test incidents to cyber and operational risks, warning vulnerabilities may crystallise together. Agenti is controlled research, not a live failure or requirement.
judgement.implication: Ask payments and resilience owners to test liquidity shock plus loss of a shared payment or orchestration service. Measure delays, containment and minimum-service recovery; record the first failed recovery step.
judgement.archiveCorrection: Revised on 18 October 2026 to correct the G7 exercise description, cite the September FPC record directly, and clarify the BeyondTrust exploitation status.

weeklyReadout.heading: Can we contain and recover from the combined effects of interacting agents?
steps: The payment simulator models system participants with different objectives and strategies.
Agents with different objectives may still react to a shared signal and shift payment timing or liquidity demand together.
Test a common liquidity shock alongside loss of a shared payment or orchestration service, then measure containment and minimum-service recovery.
Record the first recovery step that fails and assign it to the payments or resilience owner.

topSignals.title: BIS Project Agenti tests interacting agents in wholesale payment systems
topSignals.label: Financial-stability research
topSignals.why: The BIS is exploring how agents with different objectives could affect payment timing, liquidity use, gridlock and shock propagation in an auditable simulator. This is ongoing research, not a live-market result or supervisory requirement.

topSignals.title: FPC links frontier-AI incidents to cyber and operational risks
topSignals.label: Financial resilience
topSignals.why: The September Financial Policy Committee record says recent frontier-AI test-environment incidents reinforce the need for firms to prepare for cyber and operational risks. It is a direct FPC assessment, not a new requirement.
topSignals.source: Primary / Bank of England Financial Policy Committee / 2026-09-30

topSignals.title: BeyondTrust flaw is reported exploited in the wild
topSignals.label: Active exploitation
topSignals.why: The Canadian Cyber Centre reports open-source indications of exploitation in the wild. Check self-hosted Remote Support versions and apply patch BT26-05-RS where affected; the vendor says its SaaS customers were patched by 9 October.
topSignals.source: Primary / Canadian Centre for Cyber Security / 2026-10-16

topSignals.title: Hosted delivery controls need a tested fallback
topSignals.label: Hosted delivery services
topSignals.why: GitHub Status reports a 12 October disruption across Actions, pull requests and issues, separate from the 7 October incidents in Edition 17. Teams relying on hosted delivery controls should know their release fallback.

topSignals.title: European regulators link data protection with value in finance
topSignals.label: Data protection in finance
topSignals.why: CNIL, the UK ICO and Luxembourg’s CNPD say data protection and governance can affect trust, resilience, AI use and the valuation of financial data. This is joint analysis and good practice, not a new rule.
